sections.title: Macro Investment Framework and Currency Hedging
sections.content:
The foundation of successful investing lies in broad-based macro bets rather than micro-level stock picking. The instructor emphasizes that "the broader the bets that you take, the more sensible the bets that you take, the less money you will lose."

**INR Depreciation Hedge Strategy**: INR depreciation is identified as a 99% probability macro trend requiring active hedging. Primary implementation is through dollar-denominated assets (US stocks), with physical gold as an alternative. Gold ETFs are explicitly discouraged due to lack of investor control and potential future taxation changes.

**Core Investment Principle**: Success depends entirely on buying at the right price versus wrong price. This simple concept drives all subsequent strategy decisions.

![Figure: Portfolio holdings showing practical US stock allocation across tech and healthcare sectors](frame:scene_0001.jpg)

sections.title: Portfolio Allocation and Tax Optimization
sections.content:
Geographic tax residency significantly impacts investment returns and creates strategic optionality. Tax optimization becomes mandatory for portfolios exceeding ₹5-10 crore with annual transaction volumes above ₹12 crore.

**Allocation Framework by Tax Residency**:
- Indian Tax Residents: 70% India / 30% US (STCG 20%, LTCG 12.5%)
- Non-Indian Tax Residents: 50% India / 50% US minimum
- UAE Tax Residents: 0% capital gains tax creates significant alpha opportunity

**Three Critical Pre-Investment Questions**:
1. What percentage of net worth should go to US stocks and why?
2. What percentage should be ETF/mutual funds versus direct stocks?
3. How much to invest now (2-3 months) versus later?

Cash sitting in fiat currency loses 2-3% annually to inflation plus tax drag, creating opportunity cost urgency.

![Figure: Three-point portfolio decision framework showing hedge, tax, and cash allocation decisions](frame:periodic_0019.jpg)

sections.title: Market Structure and PE Multiple Analysis
sections.content:
PE ratios reflect demand-supply dynamics driven by government intervention and foreign ownership policies rather than pure fundamentals. Countries restricting foreign ownership (China, UAE) show lower PE multiples despite quality companies.

**PE Multiple Examples**:
- EMAAR (Dubai): PE of 10 (larger, established developer)
- Adani (India): PE of 50-52 (government-supported demand through DIIs)
- Nifty Index: PE of 24

Foreign ownership restrictions protect strategic assets but limit PE expansion. US and Indian markets allow foreign participation, creating speculation-driven PE expansion opportunities.

![Figure: Market structure comparison showing PE multiples across different regulatory environments](frame:periodic_0042.jpg)

sections.title: Buy-and-Forget Stock Strategy
sections.content:
Long-term buy-and-hold strategy for elite tech companies with minimal trading activity. Target 50-80% portfolio allocation in six core stocks: Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Amazon, Google, and Apple.

**Entry/Exit Rules**:
- Buy on downtrends using technical signals
- Generally do NOT sell when overvalued
- Aggregate positions on buying opportunities
- "There is just no point in exiting these stocks"

**Risk Management**: Primary risk is "buying them at the wrong price." Companies provide "enough hints before dying" through gradual decline rather than sudden collapse.

![Figure: Buy-and-forget stock categories with specific company allocations](frame:periodic_0094.jpg)

sections.title: Elite Tech Company Analysis and Value Creation
sections.content:
Elite tech companies outperform broad market indices through diversified moats and continuous innovation capability. Amazon exemplifies this through multi-industry expansion: e-commerce → advertising → cloud (AWS) → AI/robotics.

**Historical Performance**: Amazon up 11,000% versus S&P 500 up 400% over 10-15 years. Even with 30% drawdowns (2021 example), long-term trajectory remains superior.

**Meta's Social Advertising Moat**: Not social media but social advertising across Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp. AI-generated content increases rather than decreases advertising value through higher CPM and more targeting data.

**Innovation as "Tech"**: Technology represents innovation broadly across eras—Ford's assembly line (1900s), Dutch shipbuilding (1600s), modern software. Elite companies maintain competitive advantages through continuous innovation cycles.

![Figure: Amazon vs S&P 500 long-term performance comparison showing massive outperformance](frame:periodic_0116.jpg)

sections.title: Technical Analysis and Entry Timing
sections.content:
Technical analysis focuses on buying quality stocks at support levels rather than resistance, generating 3-4% definite alpha through tactical entry timing.

**Trend Definitions**:
- Uptrend: Higher highs and higher lows
- Downtrend: Lower highs and lower lows  
- Support: Price level where stock bounces repeatedly
- Resistance: Price level where stock falls repeatedly

**Entry Strategy**: Buy only at support levels, even in uptrending stocks. Avoid buying during sidetrend consolidation without directional confirmation.

**Alpha Compounding**: 2% annual alpha compounds dramatically—₹25,000 at 12% grows to ₹30 crore over 40 years, while 14% (12% + 2% alpha) grows to ₹56 crore.

![Figure: Apple chart showing support and resistance levels with proper entry points marked](frame:periodic_0143.jpg)

sections.title: Portfolio Construction and Stock Categorization
sections.content:
Practical portfolio construction involves categorizing stocks by strategy type with specific buying criteria for each category.

**Portfolio Categories**:
- **Buy-and-Forget**: META, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Amazon, Google, Apple (buy on dips)
- **High Growth**: Robotics, Fortinet, Palo Alto Networks, Coinbase, ASML, Broadcom
- **Turnaround**: Nike, LVMH, Adobe, Uber, AMD, CVS Healthcare
- **Value**: PayCom, Global Ship Lease, Novo Nordisk, Abbott Labs, Dutch Bros

Each category serves different risk/return profiles and market cycle positioning.

![Figure: Complete portfolio watchlist showing categorization by investment strategy](frame:periodic_0167.jpg)

sections.title: Valuation Analysis and Alpha Generation
sections.content:
Forward P/E analysis validates whether high-growth stocks justify their valuations. P/E ratios around 30 are acceptable for tech companies if growth rates support the multiple.

**NVIDIA Valuation Example**:
- Forward P/E: 31
- 1-year growth: 153%
- 5-year growth: 38%
- Conclusion: Valuation justified despite massive price appreciation

**Microsoft Buy Signal**: Trading 13-14% below highs after 1-year consolidation, providing tactical entry opportunity with defined risk levels.

![Figure: NVIDIA fundamental analysis showing growth rates justifying current valuation](frame:periodic_0196.jpg)

sections.title: Moving Average Trend-Following Strategy
sections.content:
Systematic trend-following using 50, 150, and 200-day moving averages to identify trend direction and reversal points.

**Uptrend Structure**: 50 DMA > 150 DMA > 200 DMA, all sloping upward
**Entry Signal**: When slopes of all three moving averages change simultaneously
**Exit Strategy**: During parabolic drops, "do nothing" or buy more; exit when trend structure reverses

**Historical Example**: Indian stock from ₹700 to ₹1,700 over 3 years (35-40% CAGR) following trend reversal signal.

**Data Quality**: Strategy works well in US markets but suffers from poor data quality in Indian markets due to excessive noise.

![Figure: NVIDIA chart showing proper moving average alignment in uptrend](frame:periodic_0215.jpg)

sections.title: Trend-Following Case Studies and Market Differences
sections.content:
US market data provides superior reliability for mechanical trend-following strategies compared to Indian markets.

**NVIDIA Case Study**: Entry at $16 trend reversal, rode uptrend to $130+, maintaining proper moving average structure throughout.

**Indian Market Limitations**: Kotak Mahindra Bank example shows excessive noise and false crossovers, making trend-following unreliable.

**Market Structure Advantage**: US markets offer transparent data and minimal regulatory interference, supporting systematic strategy implementation.

![Figure: Kotak Mahindra Bank chart showing noisy data quality in Indian markets](frame:periodic_0233.jpg)

sections.title: Risk Management and Parabolic Market Moves
sections.content:
Parabolic market drops occur over 5-7 days and cannot be timed or exited effectively. The correct response is passive acceptance or opportunistic buying with available capital.

**Parabolic Drop Management**: "You do nothing. If you have more money, you invest." Attempting to time crashes is futile due to speed and unpredictability.

**Gradual Decline Principle**: Quality companies provide warning signals before catastrophic failure through gradual deterioration rather than sudden collapse.

**Diversified Moat Protection**: Elite tech companies have multiple revenue streams, so disruption in one area doesn't destroy the entire business.

sections.title: Class Summary and Next Steps
sections.content:
The class emphasizes avoiding major investment mistakes through systematic approaches rather than maximizing returns. Key strategies include currency hedging through US stocks, tactical entry timing using technical analysis, and long-term holding of elite tech companies.

**Instructor's Track Record**:
- Mutual Fund Portfolio: 15% XIRR, 30% CAGR on pure index
- Personal Stock Portfolio: ₹2.17 crore profits booked, 18.9% CAGR from 2020

Future sessions will cover detailed ratio analysis, PEG ratios, and advanced valuation methodologies.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.content:
• **Currency Hedging**: INR depreciation is 99% probable—hedge through US stocks or physical gold, avoid gold ETFs
• **Tax Optimization**: Geographic tax residency creates significant alpha; UAE residency offers 0% capital gains
• **Portfolio Allocation**: Indian residents 70/30 India/US, non-residents minimum 50/50
• **Buy-and-Forget Strategy**: Six core stocks (Meta, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Amazon, Google, Apple) for 50-80% allocation
• **Technical Entry Timing**: Buy at support levels, not resistance—generates 3-4% alpha annually
• **Moving Average System**: 50/150/200 DMA trend-following works in US markets, poor data quality in India
• **Valuation Framework**: Forward P/E around 30 acceptable for tech if growth rates justify multiple
• **Risk Management**: Accept parabolic drops passively or buy more; quality companies decline gradually
• **Platform Setup**: Use TradingView for technical analysis, GuruFocus for fundamental validation
• **Compound Alpha**: 2% annual outperformance creates ₹26 crore additional wealth over 40 years
